Battery Boom
Battery makers are buying up every tonne of lithium coming off the pile. Demand will run well above normal for about 180 days.
Construction Slump
Building work has stalled across the region, and no new footings are going in. Iron demand drops by nearly a third for about 240 days.
Fuel Price Spike
Diesel costs have jumped across the district. Every operating mine pays about 30% more to run for 120 days.
Land Rush
Speculators are buying up claims across the district. New plot listings ask about 40% more for a year.
Seismic Survey I
A proper seismic pass gives the crew a cleaner read on the ground. Cuts survey error by a fifth.
Seismic Survey II
Denser survey lines leave the crew with fewer blind spots underfoot. Cuts survey error by a further 30%.
Core Sampling
Pulling drill core puts real rock in the trays instead of guesswork. Survey error drops by 40% more.
Efficient Extraction I
Simpler footings and a tighter site layout keep early spending lean. Cuts the cost of building a mine by 15%.
Efficient Extraction II
Standardised headframes and proven plant designs save the crew from custom fabrication. Cuts mine construction cost by a further 20%.
Mine Automation
Automated haulage keeps ore moving from the face without extra hands on shift. Cuts the daily running cost of every mine by 20%.
High-Throughput Processing I
Heavier crushers break the ore down faster at the surface. Daily output across every mine is up 25%.
Processing Line II
A second processing line runs alongside the first. Daily output is up a further 30%.
Rail Sidings and Stockpiles
Rail sidings and covered stockpiles keep the weather off the pile. Storage costs drop by 40%.
Lithium Concentrator
A concentrator plant turns raw lithium ore into saleable concentrate. Without one in place, lithium cannot be mined or sold.
